full_caption: Adaline Wraymond, Appellant, v. Evanthe Jarrowmere, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Adaline Wraymond appeals the denial by the Grayrock County Board of Adjustment of a use variance permitting operation of a transit maintenance yard at 2883 Kingfisher Drive, Grayrock, KS, a parcel zoned R-2 single-family residential.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The board's findings must be sufficient to permit meaningful review. Conclusory recitals tracking the language of the ordinance, without reference to record evidence, require remand.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: An area variance is governed by a balancing test weighing the benefit to the applicant against the detriment to the health, safety and welfare of the neighborhood, and does not require the showing of hardship applicable to use variances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The parcel is 1,240 square feet, irregular in shape, and burdened by a drainage easement across 5 percent of its buildable area. Those are conditions of the land and not of the owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Spot zoning is the singling out of a small parcel for treatment differing from that of surrounding property, for the benefit of the owner and to the detriment of the comprehensive plan. The rezoning here served a plan objective and is not spot zoning.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A use variance requires proof of unnecessary hardship: that the property cannot yield a reasonable return in any permitted use, that the hardship is unique to the parcel, and that the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Hardship must arise from the land itself and not from the owner's personal circumstances or from a self-created condition. Purchase with knowledge of the restriction is a factor but is not, standing alone, disqualifying.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Exhaustion of administrative remedies is a prerequisite to judicial review. A facial constitutional challenge to the ordinance is excepted from that requirement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Discontinuance for 6 months is presumed abandonment under Section 7.6 of the ordinance. The presumption is rebutted by proof of an intent to resume coupled with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: A nonconforming use lawfully existing at the effective date of the ordinance may continue but may not be enlarged, and is lost by abandonment or by discontinuance for the period specified in the ordinance.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Vested rights against a subsequent ordinance arise where the developer, in good-faith reliance on a validly issued permit, has made substantial expenditures. Adaline Wraymond expended $400,000 on site work before the moratorium was adopted.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: The denial is vacated and the matter remanded to the Board for findings addressing the drainage easement and the shape of the parcel.

sections.heading: RIDER A — VARIANCE APPLICATION AND FINDINGS REQUIRED
sections.text: An application for a use variance shall be granted only upon written findings, supported by substantial evidence in the record, that: (1) the property cannot yield a reasonable return in any use permitted in the district; (2) the hardship arises from conditions unique to the parcel and not generally applicable in the district; (3) the hardship was not self-created; and (4) the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality. Findings that merely recite the language of this Rider without reference to record evidence are insufficient.

sections.heading: RIDER D — VESTED RIGHTS AND MORATORIUM
sections.text: A permittee who, in good-faith reliance on a validly issued permit, has incurred substantial expenditures or substantially changed position acquires a vested right to complete the development in accordance with the permit, notwithstanding any subsequently adopted ordinance or moratorium. Expenditures for architectural, engineering and permitting services alone are not 'substantial' for purposes of this Rider unless they exceed 5 percent of the total project cost.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Kestrel.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Kestrel, the period is extended to the next business day.
